blocks.html:
Cleric

Role: Pure healer. Difficulty: Low to Medium. Weapon: Mace + Shield/Guard (Staff option for a DPS lean).

HealerSupportBeginner friendlyNear-mandatory in groups

blocks.title: Overview and role
blocks.bodyHtml:
Cleric is a near-mandatory pure healer: tanky, solo-friendly, but its tier likely dropped after a KR/TW patch.

Version note: AION 2 has been live in KR/TW since November 2025. Global PC launch is October 5, 2026, with a fully wiped Launch Scale Test on September 17-18 that does not carry over. Most Cleric guides below are KR/TW-era. A reported August 2026 balance patch cut fixed healing passives in favor of attack-power-scaling healing, reportedly pushing Cleric toward C-tier single source leprestore, date unknown1. Treat any older "S-tier healer" claim as stale.

Role and kit

Cleric wields a Mace paired with a shield or magic offhand ("Guard") for a tankier build, with a Staff option for higher magic boost and more damage oneall forum, date unknown2.

AION2 Hub describes it as a back-line healer who cycles AoE and over-time heals plus protective shields to sustain the group aion2hub, date unknown3.

  • Only class that can actively dispel debuffs, and carries the signature Summon Resurrection skill, making it near-mandatory for dungeon groups confirmed, multiple sources aion2hub, date unknown4 fextralife, date unknown5
  • Fextralife calls it "an indispensable character in party play," but says it specializes in AoE healing over single-target: "the Cleric's healing alone will not be enough" if the party ignores mechanics fextralife, date unknown6

Standing by mode

  • Party demand: very high, near-mandatory for dungeons and raids
  • PvE: strong utility pick from its heal, shield, cleanse and res kit, though the August 2026 patch reportedly weakened fixed healing passives marketing source leprestore, date unknown7
  • PvP: viable as a "survival healer" build, but reportedly slipped to C-tier alongside Chanter after the same patch single source leprestore, date unknown8
  • Solo: good. Fextralife calls it "accessible for solo players"; other guides call it tanky and safe to solo, kill speed aside, thanks to self-sustain from its own healing kit fextralife, date unknown9 mmoexp, date unknown10
Beginner tip: pick Cleric if you want a forgiving, hard-to-kill class with guaranteed group invites and don't mind managing cooldown rhythm and positioning over raw damage numbers.

blocks.title: Skill priority
blocks.headExtrasHtml: contested in detail kr-era
blocks.bodyHtml:
Keep a heal and a damage skill both leveled; the exact global-launch order is unconfirmed, so treat lists below as directional.

Gap: no reliable source found for a precise, level-by-level global-launch skill point order. The lists below are pieced together from KR/TW-era guides and should be treated as directional, not exact.
  1. Do first: keep 1-2 healing skills (Healing Light / Light of Regeneration) leveled alongside your main damage chain.
    • A Cleric with no heal rank is unplayable in groups, and one with no damage rank kills too slowly solo (synthesized from the sources below).
  2. Do first: below level 20, spec Divine Retribution 2 and 4 to leverage the spirit synergy vortexgaming, date unknown1
  3. Then (PvE, level 20+): Divine Retribution (2/3/4), Judgment Bolt (2/4/5), Sacred Energy (3/4/5), Light of Regeneration (1/4/5), Troops (2/3/4) vortexgaming, date unknown2
    • Sacred Energy is a higher DPS priority; Troops hits max DPS with a full charge.
  4. Then (PvP): shift Light of Regeneration to 1/2/5 (defense over mobility), Troops to 3/4 (full-charge windows are rarer in PvP), and Shock Release to 1/4 or 1/5 at level 16+ vortexgaming, date unknown3
  5. Later / optional: a separate arcana-tied guide orders leveling as Forge first (highest DPS), then Swift Heal, Earth's Retribution, Rain of Healing, Troops, and Lightning Judgment vortexgaming, date unknown4
    • That guide suggests reducing Light of Regeneration below level 16 to free points.

Two guides, two orders

Vortex Gaming skill-tree guide

  • Divine Retribution, Judgment Bolt, Sacred Energy, Light of Regeneration, Troops as the level 20+ PvE core vortexgaming, date unknown5

Vortex Gaming arcana-tied guide

  • Forge, Swift Heal, Earth's Retribution, Rain of Healing, Troops, Lightning Judgment, with Light of Regeneration deprioritized early vortexgaming, date unknown6

These two guides partially conflict on Light of Regeneration's priority; treat as contested, not confirmed.

Named kits

AION2 Hub names the offensive kit as Earth's Retribution, Judgment Thunder, and Divine Punishment, and the healing kit as Light of Regeneration, Healing Light, and Radiant Recovery (the grouping is this guide's; the source lists the skills without grouping them) aion2hub, date unknown7.

Playstyle: weaving damage skills between healing cycles to maintain mana efficiency. A basic solo leveling loop cited elsewhere is applying Punishment Seal, spamming Holy Strike, and healing as needed marketing, lower trust.

blocks.title: Leveling build
blocks.headExtrasHtml: Lv 1 to cap single source kr-era
blocks.bodyHtml:
Push Earth's Retribution and Heavenly Judgment first, keep Divine Grace and Earth's Blessing maxed, then take Divine Burst as your first Stigma.

This order comes from the one Inven post that frames leveling by skill-level band, cross-checked against an aggregated early-priority search summary inven 408, 2025-111.

Every "Lv" figure below is the skill's own level (its 8/12/16/20 spec breakpoints), not your character level, confirmed by a DCInside thread discussing a Stigma at "level 15" while still leveling dcinside, date unknown2.

Skill point order

StepWhenSkillTake toWhySrc
1From Lv 1Earth's Retribution (대지의 응보)Skill Lv 12 (1/3 pick)core auto-attack-cancel partner skillinven 408, 2025-11
2NextCondemnation (단죄)Skill Lv 8first skill taken in this bandinven 408, 2025-11
3NextLightning Bolt (벽력)Skill Lv 12secondary damage, priority is contested (see note)inven 408, 2025-11
4NextChain of Suffering (고통의 연쇄) and Weakening Mark (약화의 낙인)Skill Lv 12 eachstarts the paired resistance-debuff uptimeinven 408, 2025-11
5NextHeavenly Judgment (심판의 번개)Skill Lv 16 (2/5 pick)the single most important breakpoint in the rotationinven 408, 2025-11 inven 105, 2026-01
6NextHealing Light (치유의 빛)Skill Lv 16 onlytriggers Heavenly Judgment's bonus hit; do not push further yetinven 408, 2025-11 inven 19538, 2026-05
7NextBlessed Radiance (쾌유의 광휘)Skill Lv 16its spec tier once both heals are at 16inven 408, 2025-11
Two sources disagree on Lightning Bolt's priority: the leveling-era Inven post treats it as a Lv 12 pick, while a post-cap Vortex Gaming writeup calls it near-essential only at Lv 20, after a patch made full-charge use mandatory inven 408, 2025-113 vortexgaming, date unknown4. This looks patch-driven, not a real contradiction: follow the lighter Lv 12 investment while leveling, save the heavier push for after a similar patch lands globally.

The note gives no separate "leave at level 1" list; the closest equivalent is capping Warm Blessing and Healing Power Enhancement at 1-2 spare points below instead of leveling them properly.

Passives

  1. First: Divine Grace (주신의 은총), master it first, a flat attack-power passive needed for solo hunting efficiency inven 105, 2026-015
  2. Then: Earth's Blessing (대지의 은총), master alongside Divine Grace for additional attack power single source
  3. Later: Warm Blessing (따뜻한 가호) and Healing Power Enhancement (치유력 강화), only 1-2 spare points each while leveling; Healing Power Enhancement is also the single highest-priority passive on the Daevanion board inven 72, 2025-116

Level by level

  1. Lv 1-12
    Solo is damage-first: cancel Earth's Retribution into Heavenly Judgment
    • Auto-attack cancel (평캔): cancel the Earth's Retribution animation early, or rebind both skills to left/right mouse and rapid-fire them inven 408, 2025-117
    • Simpler beginner pattern reported elsewhere: apply Weakening Mark, hold a charge button, spam right-click, switch to "1" against strong enemies single source
    • Heal reactively rather than on a timer, leaning on built-in self-sustain to avoid downtime; see the Rotation and combos card below
    • Keep Divine Grace and Earth's Blessing maxed for hunting speed; see Passives above single source
  2. Lv 12
    Nezekan Daevanion board opens
    • Cooldown-reduction nodes (2.5% x2), combat-speed nodes (2.5% x2), and active-skill nodes first inven 72, 2025-118
    • Passive order: Healing Power Enhancement, then Earth's Blessing, then Divine Grace
    • Grey stat nodes in order: attack power, HP, defense, crit
  3. Lv 23
    Stigma: Divine Burst first, then Absolution (targets are Stigma levels; the Cleric unlock level is unconfirmed)
    • 권능 폭발 (Divine Burst) is the earliest pick, at Stigma Lv 1 inven 408, 2025-119; a later post-cap thread rates a similarly named skill avoid-tier, possibly a balance change contested inven 105, date unknown10
    • 면죄 (Absolution) follows at Stigma Lv 5, then 10, for cleanse plus heal utility; a DCInside thread shows a player choosing between Absolution and Salvation at Stigma Lv 15, so both are viable early picks dcinside, date unknown11
    • Light of Protection (보호의 빛) reaches Stigma Lv 10 while leveling inven 408, 2025-1112, later the highest-adoption endgame Stigma at 92.7% cielui, 2026-0913
    • Eustiel's Authority (유스티엘의 권능) reaches Stigma Lv 5 while leveling inven 408, 2025-1114
  4. At cap
    Respec before dungeons: drop Absolution, push the healing spread
    1. Heavenly Judgment (심판의 번개) to Skill Lv 16 inven 657, 2026-0115
    2. Blessed Radiance (쾌유의 광휘) to Skill Lv 16
    3. Healing Light (치유의 빛) to Skill Lv 16
    4. Regeneration Light (재생의 빛) to Skill Lv 16
    5. Blessed Radiance again to Skill Lv 20, funded by removing the Absolution Stigma
    • Keep the damage kit above these floors too: Earth's Retribution at least Lv 12, Heavenly Judgment at least Lv 16, Condemnation at least Lv 16 inven 657, 2026-0116
    • See the Skill priority, Stigma picks and Daevanion board route cards above and below for the full endgame spread.
Avoid: pushing Healing Light or Regeneration Light past their early breakpoints while soloing. Take Healing Light to Lv 16 only, since that is where it triggers the Heavenly Judgment bonus hit, and heavier heal investment this early is reported to slow solo growth single source inven 408, 2025-1117

Dropped from this card: "Gear while leveling", since the note found no sourced facts beyond what the Gear and stat priority card below already documents.

blocks.title: Stigma picks
blocks.bodyHtml:
Level Earth's Punishment to 20 first; beyond that, two guides disagree on names, and unlock-level claims are single-source.

What stigmas are

Stigmas are advanced skills separate from your leveling tree, funded with Stigma Shards instead of Skill Points, equipped in a limited number of slots (6 in the KR-era cap) expcarry, date unknown1.

  • A general AION 2 stigma-system explainer: complete a level-20 campaign quest to begin using Stigma Stones single source boostroom, date unknown2
    • Slots open automatically at further level thresholds.
    • This source is written specifically about AION 2, not the original Aion, though it doesn't caveat KR-versus-global differences.
  • A weaker, Korean community signal says two additional advanced stigma slots open at level 45. This is a slot-count claim only, and the source thread could not be isolated, so treat it as unconfirmed single source, weakly sourced

Level 45 advanced stigma list (Korean Cleric board)

A Korean Cleric-board thread on 상급스티그마 선택 (advanced stigma selection) recommends this set, all to level 25 unless noted single source kr-era inven, date unknown3:

  • 대지의징벌 (Earth's Punishment)
  • 보호의빛 (Protection's Light)
  • 고결한기운 (Noble Energy), scales better for damage at levels 20-25 than Amplified Prayer
  • 증폭의기도 (Amplified Prayer), to level 23 only, whose main benefit is a 1.5-second duration increase

Two guides, different names

Two guides give different core stigma lists for the same class; treat this section as contested in naming even though the general shape (PvE = group sustain, PvP = personal survival) agrees.

Guide A (Vortex Gaming, via search summary)

  • PvE: Light of Protection (15), Earth Punishment (20), Amplification Prayer (15, fixed), Ruin (15), Summon Resurrection (5), Salvation (15, situational) single source
  • PvP: Exemption (15), Salvation (15), Yustiel (15-20, fixed), Summon Resurrection (5), Ruin (15), Earth Punishment (20, situational)

Guide B (Vortex Gaming, direct fetch)

  • PvE "Core Four": Power of Life, Earth's Punishment, Noble Aura, Light of Possession vortexgaming, date unknown4
  • Dungeon add-ons: Salvation for Hall of Illusions (grouped laser pattern survivability); Salvation + Power of Uriel for Sanctuary
  • PvP party: Summoned Hatchling, Power of Uriel, Power of Life/Absolution, Light of Possession
  • PvP solo: Light of Possession, Power of Uriel, Noble Aura, Power of Life, Salvation

Both guides agree Earth's Punishment leveled to 20 is a near-universal pick, and that PvP swaps in more personal-survival stigmas (Salvation, Power of Uriel/Yustiel) versus PvE's group-sustain focus.

Naming differences like "Light of Protection" vs "Power of Life" may be translation or patch-version drift rather than confirmed distinct skills contested.

A Korean-language community summary (titles found via search, not directly fetched, single source) lists these party-heal stigmas, covering cleanse, defense/attack buffs, resistance buffs, and move-speed boosts:

  • 면죄 (Exemption/Absolution)
  • 치유의 기운 (Healing Energy)
  • 보호의 빛 (Light of Protection)
  • 유스티엘의 권능 (Power of Yustiel)
Beginner tip: spend Stigma Shards first on stigmas already equipped in your main rotation before funding alternates, and pick ones that unlock a specialization effect at a reachable level over spreading thin expcarry, date unknown5.

blocks.title: Daevanion board route
blocks.bodyHtml:
Build one full rotation on Mastery skills first, then fund the Daevanion nodes that support it; no Cleric-specific route is confirmed.

The Daevanion board is a node-investment system spent with Daevanion Points, gated by character level. This is a general system note, not Cleric-specific expcarry, date unknown1.

  1. Lv 12
    Nezekan board unlocks

    Start spending Daevanion Points.

  2. Lv 20
    Zikel board unlocks
  3. Lv 30
    Vaizel board unlocks
  4. Lv 40
    Triniel board unlocks
  5. Lv 45
    Four advanced boards unlock

    Ariel, Azphel, Marchutan, Yustiel.

Node costs and route

  • Node cost tiers (general system): Grey (stat) 1 point, Green (passive skill) 2 points, Blue (active skill) 3 points, Orange (unique skill) 4 points single source aggregation
  • Recommended early route, not Cleric-exclusive: prioritize Blue (active skill) nodes early for immediate combat power
  • For a healer specifically: prioritize your main damage chain skill and any node that boosts an HP-recovery skill or a skill usable while moving
Gap: no reliable source found for a Cleric-specific, node-by-node Daevanion route naming actual nodes on any board.

Resets

Individual nodes or the whole board can reportedly be reset, at a KR-era cost of about 500 Kinah per node, explicitly flagged as "subject to change on Global" expcarry, date unknown2.

General guidance: build one full rotation on Mastery skills first, fund the Stigmas used in that rotation, trace the cheapest Daevanion path that supports the same build, and only reset when your role changes meaningfully.

Daevanion Points and Crystals come from leveling/quests, achievements, and content activities expcarry, date unknown3.

blocks.title: Arcana
blocks.bodyHtml:
Fill Chalice with damage/heal skills, prioritize Divine Grace on Bell and Healing Power Boost on Mirror, and lock old cards instead of deleting them.

Card types

Arcana cards come in types referenced as Chalice, Bell, Mirror, and Scales vortexgaming, date unknown1:

  • Chalice: aim for 2+ of these skills on one card - Forge, Swift Heal, Earth's Retribution, Rain of Healing, Troops, Lightning Judgment vortexgaming, date unknown2
  • Bell: priority order is Divine Grace (minimum level 3), then Shield of Immortality, then Warm Aura
  • Mirror: priority is Healing Power Boost first (target level 4), then Earth's Blessing second (target level 3), which improves critical-damage scaling
  • Scales: get at least 2 useful active skills on the card since it "heavily influences your overall setup direction"

A separate AI-summarized search result for the same underlying guide family gives a near-identical Bell/Mirror/Scales list, cross-confirming the above.

Setup and cost strategy

When synthesizing Chalice cards, check 2 roll options if affordable; for other card types, 1 option is enough to save resources. For general bonus sets, favor "Frenzy 4 Pure" or "History 4 Pure" over "Vitality," since Vitality cards are expensive and not worth chasing unless already owned.

Avoid: deleting old Arcana cards when the meta shifts. Lock them instead, since balance patches can bring old cards back into relevance. Don't sink heavy resources into Vitality-type cards from scratch vortexgaming, date unknown3.
Gap: no reliable source found confirming whether "Chalice, Bell, Mirror, Scales" are the actual Global localization terms or a fan/KR-guide translation. Treat the names as provisional pending Global client confirmation.

blocks.title: Gear and stat priority
blocks.bodyHtml:
Go Healing Power, HP, Defense, Magic Boost for pure support; swap to a DPS/support pair of gear sets at endgame.

Weapon: Mace + Shield/Guard offhand for survivability-focused solo leveling and tanky healing; Staff for higher magic boost and faster kill speed on a DPS-hybrid lean oneall forum, date unknown1.

  1. Do first (pure support/healer): Healing Power, HP, Defense, Magic Boost pvpbank, date unknown2
  2. Then (tanky support variant): HP, Healing Power, Magic Resist, Defense.
  3. Later / optional (raid-healer example build): a sample stat spread from a community build aion2hub, date unknown3
    • Willpower as primary stat (410), plus Intelligence
    • HP (~28,197), MP (~7,302), Defense (~18,798)
    • Roughly -18% MP cost and ~28.4% regeneration; the author labels this "an orientative test build, tune to your group and gear."

Stat callouts

  • AoE Healing Boost amplifies the primary healer role directly
  • Shield Strength reduces MP spent on healing
  • Cooldown Reduction increases uptime on key heal/shield skills
  • Debuff Cleanse enhancements matter for high-end dungeons and raids marketing aggregation aoeah, date unknown4
Gap: no reliable source found specifying exactly which gear slot to enhance first. The example build above enhanced weapon and offhand to +20/+5 alongside a matching full "Splendent Nemesis Dragon Lord" armor set (+20 each, set bonus "Indomitable Dedication 6pc"), suggesting a full-set approach, but this is one anecdotal build, not a stated rule.

Gear swapping

At endgame some players keep two sets, one for magic attack/DPS and one for support with Healing Boost, swapping depending on whether they are actively healing or contributing damage single source, marketing pvpbank, date unknown5.

Gap: no Cleric-specific manastone socket priority was found. The only manastone information located is a general cross-class mechanic, gear ships with locked manastone slots, unlocked via Manastone Fasteners obtained from gear extraction, sourced from an original-Aion fan wiki and not confirmed to apply identically to AION 2 kr-era aion fandom, date unknown6. Still no reliable AION-2-specific, Cleric-specific manastone guidance found.

blocks.title: Rotation and combos
blocks.bodyHtml:
Solo, apply Punishment Seal and spam Holy Strike; in a party, cycle heals and shields proactively rather than firefighting damage.

Solo PvE loop

  1. Apply Punishment Seal.
  2. Spam Holy Strike as your main damage filler.
  3. Heal as needed rather than on a fixed timer.

Earth's Retribution and Judgment Thunder let Cleric chip in meaningful ranged damage and sustain its own mana while healing aion2hub, date unknown1.

Party and support rhythm

Cleric does not spam heals constantly; it follows a rhythm confirmed, qualitative: cycling AoE and over-time heals, layering shields proactively, and cleansing debuffs rather than firefighting single-target damage.

Fextralife: the Cleric specializes in Area of Effect healing rather than single-target support, and gameplay is bouncing between different healing sources while weaving in damaging skills fextralife, date unknown2.

Many heals (e.g. Healing Light) can be charged for a stronger effect at the cost of higher MP and cast time.

Beginner tip: use shield skills like Immortal Curtain (absorbs a fixed amount for up to 10 seconds per Fextralife) proactively before a known boss mechanic hits, not reactively after damage lands.

Macro layout

Suggested layout: Charge on Q, all three healing skills bound together on Num 1, instant attack skills on Num 2, Stigma skills spread across Num 5-8 keyran, date unknown3.

The same source cautions that most veteran players keep healing and buff macros manual rather than fully macroed, since heal/buff timing precision matters more than raw damage-chain speed.

Gap: no reliable source found for a confirmed auto-hunt skill setup specific to Cleric.

blocks.title: Leveling notes
blocks.bodyHtml:
Cleric levels safely and comfortably solo thanks to self-healing, but kills slower than true DPS classes.

Solo leveling comfort rates positively across sources: Cleric is "tanky and safe to play solo" and, unlike a stereotypical helpless solo healer, has enough offensive tools to handle solo content while maintaining excellent sustain marketing, lower trust u4n, date unknown1.

Its self-heal (e.g. Healing Light) means less time on potions or downtime between fights.

Kill speed is slower than true DPS classes; the tradeoff is durability and near-zero death risk while leveling.

Gap: no reliable source found with specific pull-size or mob-density numbers for Cleric, and none identifying a specific level or gear milestone where Cleric's power spikes. General guides only say the class stays viable and safe throughout leveling.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.bodyHtml:
Stay active and mobile: shield before damage lands, swap Stigmas by content, and don't lean on burst heals to fix mechanics.

Do

  • Apply offensive pressure during downtime instead of only reacting to damage mmoexp, date unknown1
  • Call out repositioning so AoE heals land on a grouped party
  • Use shields proactively before a known burst ("Immortal Curtain is proactive, not reactive")
  • Balance Skill Points between damage and healing kits rather than dumping into one
  • Swap Stigma loadouts by content (PvE party, PvE solo, PvP), per Korean community guidance ("don't stick to one setup, must swap by content")
  • Lock old Arcana cards instead of deleting them when the meta shifts vortexgaming, date unknown2
  • Stay mobile while healing to dodge avoidable boss/PvP attacks

Do not

  • Play as a purely passive, reactive healer mmoexp, date unknown3
  • Heal when nobody needs it, wasting MP and triggering long cooldowns early in a fight
  • Assume AoE heals land when the party is spread out too far
  • Rely on burst single-target healing to fix every mechanic mistake, "the Cleric's healing alone will not be enough" fextralife, date unknown4
  • Use shields reactively after damage already landed
  • Stand still while healing instead of staying mobile
